injectables.description:
Service to create Overlays. Overlays are dynamically added pieces of floating UI, meant to be used as a low-level building building block for other components. Dialogs, tooltips, menus, selects, etc. can all be built using overlays. The service should primarily be used by authors of re-usable components rather than developers building end-user applications.

An overlay is a PortalHost, so any kind of Portal can be loaded into one.

  </ng-container>
  <ng-container *ngSwitchCase="'currency'">
    <dx-flex-currency *ngIf="!isBusy;else showTextLoader" [data]="source?.data[column?.field]"
      [setting]="column?.setting?.currency" [column]="column">
    </dx-flex-currency>
  </ng-container>
  <ng-container *ngSwitchCase="'date'">
    <dx-flex-date *ngIf="!isBusy;else showTextLoader" [data]="source?.data[column?.field]"
      [setting]="column?.setting?.date"></dx-flex-date>
  </ng-container>
  <ng-container *ngSwitchCase="'action'">
    <dx-flex-action [isBusy]="isBusy" (onExpand)="onExpandToggle($event)" (onExternalAction)="externalAction($event)"
      [selectedData]="expandData" [data]="source" [columns]="column">
    </dx-flex-action>
  </ng-container>
  <ng-container *ngSwitchCase="'avatar'">
    <dx-flex-avatar *ngIf="!isBusy;else AvatarSkeletonLoader" [column]="column" [data]="source?.ngDxAvatar">
    </dx-flex-avatar>
  </ng-container>
  <ng-container *ngSwitchCase="'input'">
    <dx-flex-input *ngIf="!isBusy;else showTextLoader" [(ngModel)]="source?.data[column?.field]" [key]="column?.field"
      (onUpdate)="updateInput()" [setting]="source?.input"></dx-flex-input>
  </ng-container>
  <ng-container *ngSwitchCase="'select'">
    <dx-flex-select *ngIf="!isBusy;else showTextLoader" [(ngModel)]="source?.data[column?.field]"
      (onUpdate)="updateInput()" [setting]="source?.selectSetting"></dx-flex-select>
  </ng-container>
  <ng-container *ngSwitchCase="'avatar_group'">
    <dx-flex-avatar *ngIf="!isBusy;else AvatarSkeletonLoader" [column]="column" [data]="source?.ngDxAvatar">
    </dx-flex-avatar>
  </ng-container>
  <ng-container *ngSwitchCase="'multi_chip'">
    <dx-flex-multi-chip *ngIf="!isBusy;else chipSkeletonLoader" [column]="column" [data]="source?.multiChip">
    </dx-flex-multi-chip>
  </ng-container>

  <ng-container *ngSwitchDefault>
    <dx-flex-table-text-cell></dx-flex-table-text-cell>
  </ng-container>
</ng-container>

components.template:
Pages in Storybook

We recommend building UIs with a component-driven process starting with atomic components and ending with pages.

Render pages with mock data. This makes it easy to build and review page states without needing to navigate to them in your app. Here are some handy patterns for managing page data in Storybook:

  • Use a higher-level connected component. Storybook helps you compose such data from the "args" of child component stories
  • Assemble data in the page component from your services. You can mock these services out using Storybook.

Get a guided tutorial on component-driven development at Storybook tutorials . Read more in the docs .

Tip Adjust the width of the canvas with the Viewports addon in the toolbar
